# Project Management Plan

## 1. Project Charter

**Project name:** Local Library Event Booking MVP  
**Project sponsor:** Library Operations Director  
**Project manager:** Part-time PM  
**Delivery window:** 8 weeks  
**Budget cap:** $24,000

### Purpose
Deliver a lightweight web MVP that allows residents to browse library events and reserve seats online, while giving library staff a simple admin view to track bookings and attendance.

### Business objective
- Reduce manual phone/email bookings by at least 50% within 2 months of launch.
- Improve event visibility and booking convenience for residents.
- Provide staff with a basic operational reporting capability.

### Deliverables
- Public event list page
- Event details page
- Reservation form with seat limits
- In-app/email confirmation message mock
- Admin dashboard for viewing bookings
- Basic booking report by event
- Test results summary
- Deployment guide
- Handoff documentation

### Success criteria
- MVP launched by end of week 8
- Budget variance under 5%
- 95%+ of critical test cases pass before launch
- Staff can manage at least 10 pilot events
- At least 20 pilot bookings completed successfully during UAT

## 2. Scope Definition

### In scope
- Responsive web MVP
- Event browsing and detail views
- Reservation workflow with seat capacity enforcement
- Staff admin booking overview
- Basic reporting for booked seats per event
- QA, deployment instructions, handoff docs

### Out of scope
- Payments
- Waitlist automation
- SMS notifications
- Multi-branch support
- Native mobile app
- CRM or external system integrations

### Constraints
- One developer limits parallel engineering work
- Low-maintenance technology stack required
- Accessibility must meet WCAG AA awareness level
- Fixed budget cap of $24,000

### Assumptions
- Hosting already exists
- Staff can handle edge cases manually during pilot
- No complex integrations needed for MVP

## 3. Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

1. **Initiation & Planning**
   1.1 Confirm requirements and success metrics  
   1.2 Approve scope and backlog  
   1.3 Finalize schedule and budget baseline  
   1.4 Kickoff meeting

2. **Design**
   2.1 User flows for resident booking  
   2.2 Admin dashboard wireframes  
   2.3 Visual design and accessibility review  
   2.4 Design signoff

3. **Build**
   3.1 Project setup and architecture  
   3.2 Event list page  
   3.3 Event detail page  
   3.4 Reservation form and validation  
   3.5 Seat limit logic  
   3.6 Admin dashboard  
   3.7 Basic reporting  
   3.8 Confirmation flow

4. **Testing & Quality**
   4.1 Test plan and test cases  
   4.2 Functional testing  
   4.3 Accessibility checks  
   4.4 Defect fixes and regression testing  
   4.5 UAT with staff pilot users

5. **Launch & Handoff**
   5.1 Deployment checklist  
   5.2 Production launch  
   5.3 Staff training/handoff  
   5.4 Post-launch monitoring  
   5.5 Lessons learned

## 4. Schedule Baseline

| Week | Focus | Key milestones |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Planning and requirements | Charter approved, backlog confirmed |
| 2 | UX/UI design | Wireframes complete |
| 3 | Design finalization + setup | Design signoff, technical setup complete |
| 4 | Core public pages build | Event list and detail pages done |
| 5 | Booking workflow build | Reservation flow and seat logic complete |
| 6 | Admin/reporting build | Admin dashboard and reports complete |
| 7 | QA and UAT | Critical defects resolved, pilot UAT starts |
| 8 | Launch and handoff | Go-live, documentation and training complete |

### Milestones
- M1: Charter and scope approval — end of Week 1
- M2: Design approval — end of Week 3
- M3: Feature complete — end of Week 6
- M4: UAT signoff — mid Week 8
- M5: Production launch — end of Week 8

### Dependencies
- Design signoff before full UI build
- Reservation logic before QA end-to-end tests
- Admin dashboard depends on booking data model completion
- UAT depends on stable feature-complete build

### Critical path
Requirements approval → design signoff → booking workflow build → admin/reporting completion → QA/UAT → launch

## 5. Resource Plan

| Role | Allocation | Timing | Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product Manager | Part-time | Weeks 1-8 | Scope, stakeholder alignment, status, UAT coordination |
| Full-stack Developer | Full-time | Weeks 1-8 | Build, fixes, deployment support |
| Designer | Part-time | Weeks 1-3 | UX, UI, accessibility-aware designs |
| QA Contractor | Part-time | Weeks 6-8 | Test planning, execution, regression, UAT support |

### Capacity notes
- Developer is the primary bottleneck; avoid adding unnecessary scope.
- PM should protect focus by batching stakeholder feedback.
- QA should begin test preparation before full handoff in Week 6.

## 6. Budget Baseline

| Cost item | Estimate |
|---|---:|
| Full-stack developer | $14,000 |
| Product manager (part-time) | $4,000 |
| Designer (part-time, 3 weeks) | $2,500 |
| QA contractor (part-time, 3 weeks) | $2,500 |
| Contingency reserve | $1,000 |
| **Total** | **$24,000** |

### Budget controls
- Weekly burn review
- Scope change approval required if contingency use exceeds 50%
- No new features added after Week 5 without sponsor approval

## 7. Risk Register

| ID | Risk | Probability | Impact | Response/Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Single developer becomes bottleneck | High | High | Prioritize MVP-only scope, freeze scope early, PM removes blockers quickly | PM |
| R2 | Accessibility gaps found late | Medium | High | Include accessibility checks in design and QA, use simple components | Designer/QA |
| R3 | Stakeholder feedback causes scope creep | Medium | High | Formal change control, backlog triage, sponsor signoff on changes | PM |
| R4 | UAT uncovers critical booking defects | Medium | High | Start QA prep early, test core flow first, reserve contingency for fixes | Dev/QA |
| R5 | Reporting/admin needs are underestimated | Medium | Medium | Validate staff workflows in Week 1, keep admin features minimal | PM |
| R6 | Launch delayed by deployment issues | Low | Medium | Create deployment checklist and dry run before go-live | Dev |
| R7 | Lower-than-expected pilot adoption | Low | Medium | Coordinate pilot users early and provide staff guidance | Sponsor/PM |

### Top risk actions this cycle
- Finalize requirements in Week 1
- Run accessibility review before development starts
- Lock MVP scope by end of Week 2
- Prepare smoke test and deployment checklist by Week 6

## 8. Issue and Change Control

### Issue process
1. Log issue
2. Assess severity and schedule impact
3. Assign owner and due date
4. Track to closure in weekly review

### Change control
- Any feature request affecting timeline or budget requires PM review.
- Material changes require sponsor approval.
- Changes after Week 5 are deferred unless required for launch readiness.

## 9. Stakeholder Matrix

| Stakeholder | Role | Interest | Influence | Needs | Engagement approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Library Operations Director | Sponsor | High | High | Delivery confidence, budget/status visibility | Weekly summary, milestone approvals |
| Library staff coordinators | Internal users | High | Medium | Easy admin workflow, accurate booking data | Workshops, UAT sessions, training |
| Residents | End users | High | Low | Simple booking experience, clear confirmations | Usability-focused design and pilot feedback |
| Delivery team | Execution | High | Medium | Clear priorities, quick decisions, low churn | Standups, weekly planning/review |

## 10. Communication Plan

| Audience | Content | Frequency | Channel | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sponsor | Progress, risks, budget, decisions | Weekly | Email/status summary | PM |
| Delivery team | Tasks, blockers, priorities | 2-3x weekly | Standup/chat | PM |
| Staff coordinators | Feature previews, workflow validation | Biweekly | Demo/workshop | PM |
| UAT participants | Test instructions, issue follow-up | During Weeks 7-8 | Email/shared doc | QA/PM |

### Reporting cadence
- Weekly RAG-style project status
- Milestone reviews at end of Weeks 1, 3, 6, and 8
- Immediate escalation for any risk threatening launch date or budget cap

## 11. Quality Plan

### Quality objectives
- Core booking journey works end-to-end
- Seat limits enforced accurately
- Admin can view bookings reliably
- Accessibility issues minimized before launch
- Critical defects resolved before go-live

### Quality gates
- Requirements signoff complete
- Design reviewed for accessibility and usability
- Feature-complete build by end of Week 6
- 95%+ critical test pass rate
- Sponsor/UAT signoff before launch

## 12. Project Health Baseline

### Initial health assessment
- **Scope:** Green, clearly defined for MVP
- **Schedule:** Amber, due to single-developer dependency
- **Budget:** Green, feasible if scope is controlled
- **Resources:** Amber, limited redundancy
- **Risk:** Amber, manageable with strong scope discipline
- **Stakeholder alignment:** Green, provided Week 1 validation occurs

## 13. Success Metrics and Tracking

| Metric | Target | Tracking method |
|---|---|---|
| On-time delivery | Launch by end of Week 8 | Milestone tracking |
| Budget variance | < 5% | Weekly burn review |
| Scope creep | < 10% | Change log vs baseline scope |
| Critical test pass rate | >= 95% | QA test report |
| Pilot operational readiness | 10 events managed by staff | UAT checklist |
| Pilot booking success | 20 successful bookings | UAT/pilot booking log |
| Manual booking reduction | 50% in 2 months | Post-launch operations review |

## 14. Immediate Next Steps

1. Confirm requirements and admin workflow with staff in kickoff.
2. Approve scope baseline and explicitly defer out-of-scope requests.
3. Finalize backlog and acceptance criteria by end of Week 1.
4. Schedule design review and accessibility check in Week 2.
5. Set weekly status and risk review cadence.

## 15. Executive Summary

This project is achievable within 8 weeks and the $24,000 cap if scope remains tightly controlled and the team protects the single developer from churn. The main delivery risks are resource bottleneck, late accessibility findings, and scope creep. A disciplined MVP approach, early staff validation, and strong QA/UAT focus should enable successful launch and handoff.
